## Purpose
Recognises a response blocked by an edge proxy (Cloudflare bot protection) rather than by the target service, so diagnostics and deploys do not misreport it as "credentials rejected".

## Responsibilities
- **`_CHALLENGE_MARKERS`:** `_cf_chl_opt`, `challenge-platform`, `cf-browser-verification`, `<title>Just a moment...</title>`, `Attention Required! | Cloudflare`.
- **`EDGE_BLOCK_ADVICE`:** a fixed paragraph telling the user to add a WAF custom rule that skips bot and challenge checks for the deploy and health paths (or the backend IP), or to turn off Bot Fight Mode / Under Attack mode; for Cloudflare Access, to send `CF-Access-Client-Id` / `CF-Access-Client-Secret` as custom headers. Copy it verbatim.
- **`edge_block(resp)`:**
  - returns None unless the status is 403, 429 or 503;
  - flags the response when the `cf-mitigated` header is "challenge", or when the `server` header contains "cloudflare" and one of the markers is in the first 6000 chars of the body;
  - returns "HTTP <code> — blocked by Cloudflare bot protection (ray <cf-ray>)".

## Key elements
`edge_block`, `EDGE_BLOCK_ADVICE`.

## Control flow
A pure function.

## Data, state and side effects
None.

## Configuration
None.

## Interactions
- **Used by:** `checks._check_http` (the health and endpoint probes) and `deployers._deploy_over_http`.

## Error handling and edge cases
- An undecodable body falls back to checking the headers only.

## Nuances and gotchas
- **`cf-mitigated: challenge` alone is enough.** The `server` header is only needed for the body-marker test.
- **A challenge means the service never saw the request,** so no credentials were checked.

## How to rebuild this file
1. Write the module docstring (why it exists).
2. Copy the marker tuple and the advice text exactly.
3. Write `edge_block` as described.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_edge_block.py`. It checks that a Cloudflare challenge is recognised and that a real auth failure is not mistaken for one.
